questions.q: Why capture the actual execution plan rather than the estimated plan when troubleshooting a real performance problem?
options: Actual plans include real row counts, and estimated-vs-actual row counts diverging sharply is itself one of the clearest signs of a stale statistics problem
Estimated plans are always more accurate than actual plans
Actual plans can only be captured on Azure SQL Managed Instance
There is no difference between the two plan types
questions.explain: Include Actual Execution Plan (Ctrl+M) runs the query and shows what really happened, not just what the optimizer predicted.

questions.q: In a graphical execution plan, what does the cost percentage on each operator represent?
options: That operator's relative share of the total query cost, with all operators in the batch summing to 100%
The exact number of milliseconds that operator took to run
The percentage of disk space the query is using
A fixed value that never changes between runs
questions.explain: The operator with the highest cost percentage is where the optimizer thinks the most relative time is going.

questions.q: What does a thick arrow feeding into a small downstream operator usually indicate?
options: A large number of rows were read and then thrown away downstream -- wasted I/O worth investigating
The query is already perfectly optimized
The arrow thickness is purely cosmetic and carries no information
The operator ran instantly with zero rows
questions.explain: Arrow thickness encodes row count -- a thick arrow narrowing sharply is a red flag worth investigating.

questions.q: In which direction does a graphical execution plan read?
options: Right to left, top to bottom -- data flows from scan operators on the right toward SELECT on the far left
Left to right only
Bottom to top only
Plans have no consistent reading direction
questions.explain: Scan/seek operators sit on the right where data enters the plan; the final SELECT sits on the far left.

questions.q: How does this lesson build on T-SQL Development's coverage of execution plans (Lesson 90) and SET STATISTICS TIME/IO (Lessons 91-92)?
options: It goes from scans-vs-seeks on a query you're actively writing to reading a full graphical plan, under pressure, for a query you didn't write and don't yet know what's wrong with
It completely replaces the need to ever run SET STATISTICS TIME or IO again
It re-teaches scans vs. seeks from scratch with no new content
T-SQL Development never covered execution plans at any level
questions.explain: This lesson is explicitly the DBA-level depth on the same underlying skill introduced in T-SQL Development.
